paper.title_en: Quantum shifted inverse iteration for local eigenpair extraction
paper.abstract_en: Computing eigenpairs of Hermitian matrices is fundamental in physics and numerical analysis. We develop quantum shifted inverse iteration algorithms for local eigenpair extraction. First, block encoding and quantum singular value transformation enable estimation of the eigenvalue closest to a prescribed shift and preparation of its eigenstate, offering a potential exponential improvement in matrix dimension dependence under suitable assumptions. Second, when no external shift is available, we propose an initial-state Rayleigh quotient variant that coherently incorporates the shift into a block encoding, avoiding explicit statistical estimation. Furthermore, to exploit refined spectral information from subsequent iterates, we extend this approach to a two-stage scheme combining initial coherent shift construction, finite explicit Rayleigh quotient updates, and fixed shift refinement to limit additional computational costs. Small scale simulations illustrate the expected behavior in tested examples.
